_documentation.description: Project Nyra - Ultimate Enhanced Settings Configuration
_documentation.purpose: This settings file orchestrates Claude-Flow with complete memory system integration including RuVector (fast vector search), Letta (agent memory), Graphiti (temporal knowledge graphs), FalkorDB (graph database), Mem0 (user personalization), and OpenMemory (cross-app profiles). The configuration is designed for a 4-PC setup with GPU workers and emphasizes performance through caching, batching, and neural optimization.
_documentation.architecture: Hybrid local GPU + cloud API routing with intelligent fallback
_documentation.memory_hierarchy: RuVector (fast retrieval) → Letta (agent state) → Graphiti (temporal tracking) → Mem0 (user profiles)

env._comment_env: Environment variables control the fundamental operating behavior of Claude-Flow. These settings determine whether the system operates as an orchestrator (main PC) or worker (GPU machines), how aggressive the optimization should be, and whether features like auto-commit and GitHub integration are enabled.
env._comment_memory_systems: The following environment variables control which memory systems are active. You can enable multiple systems simultaneously as they serve different purposes. RuVector handles fast vector search, Letta manages agent memory state, Graphiti tracks temporal changes, and Mem0/OpenMemory handle user personalization.

performance._comment_performance: Performance configuration is critical for your 4-PC setup where you want to maximize the use of your local GPU workers while maintaining responsiveness. The aggressive caching strategy stores frequently accessed data in memory, reducing API calls to both local and cloud models. Parallelization allows multiple operations to run simultaneously across your GPU workers, significantly speeding up batch operations and complex workflows.

caching._comment_caching: Separate cache configurations for different subsystems allow fine-tuned control over memory usage and invalidation policies. The hooks cache stores command patterns, neural cache stores model predictions, and memory cache stores frequently accessed memory blocks. TTL (time-to-live) values are in milliseconds and determine how long data stays fresh before re-fetching.

parallelization._comment_parallelization: Parallelization settings determine how many operations can run simultaneously. With maxConcurrent set to 20 and 8 worker threads, the system can handle substantial parallel workloads. The task queue size of 500 ensures operations don't get dropped during peak usage, and priority levels allow critical tasks to jump ahead of less important ones.

pooling._comment_pooling: Agent pooling pre-spawns agents so they're ready when needed, eliminating startup latency. Different agent types have different pool sizes based on expected usage patterns. Coordinators are used frequently but need few instances, while coders are heavily used and benefit from a larger pool. The recycleAfter setting prevents memory leaks by retiring agents after they've handled a certain number of tasks.

memory._comment_memory: The unified memory configuration coordinates all five memory systems working together. Auto-persist ensures changes are saved immediately, compression reduces storage costs, and the sync interval determines how often memory systems exchange data. Each system has its own namespace to prevent conflicts, and retention policies ensure compliance with data protection regulations while keeping storage manageable.
memory._comment_systems: The systems configuration defines how each memory system integrates with Claude-Flow. RuVector provides fast vector search for code and documentation, Letta maintains agent state across sessions, Graphiti tracks temporal changes in loan applications and borrower information, FalkorDB stores the graph database backend, and Mem0/OpenMemory handle user personalization that follows borrowers across different applications.

coordination._comment_coordination: Memory system coordination ensures all five systems work together harmoniously without conflicts or data duplication. The sync strategy determines how frequently systems exchange data, conflict resolution handles cases where different systems have different versions of the same data, and cross-system queries allow complex operations that span multiple memory types (for example, finding all borrowers who match a vector search AND have specific temporal state changes in Graphiti).

permissions._comment_permissions: Permission management is critical for security and preventing accidental destructive operations. The allow list explicitly permits safe operations like running Claude-Flow commands, Git operations, and MCP tool access. The deny list prevents dangerous commands that could damage the system. Auto-approve settings allow certain trusted tools to run without user confirmation, speeding up automated workflows.

hooks._comment_hooks_overview: The hooks system provides lifecycle event handling throughout Claude-Flow operations. Hooks trigger automatically at specific points (session start, before/after tool use, on errors, etc.) and can execute commands, update memory, train neural models, and create checkpoints. This creates a comprehensive audit trail while also enabling self-optimization through continuous learning.

_optimization._comment: Hook optimization settings control batching and parallelization of hook execution. When batch is true, multiple hooks can be combined into a single execution context, reducing overhead. Parallel execution allows independent hooks to run simultaneously. Caching prevents redundant hook executions for identical inputs, and deduplication removes duplicate commands from the execution queue.

hooks.command: infisical run --projectId="8374cea9-e5e8-4050-bda4-b91f25ab30ef" --env="dev" --path="/shared" -- claude mcp start
hooks._comment: This hook automatically starts all MCP servers with secrets loaded from Infisical. This ensures sensitive API keys are never committed to Git while still being available to all services that need them.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha hooks pre-command --command "$CLAUDE_COMMAND" --validate-safety true --prepare-resources true --predict-outcome true --check-patterns true --batch true --cache true
hooks._comment: Before executing any bash command, this hook validates safety, prepares necessary resources, predicts the outcome using neural models, and checks against known problematic patterns. This prevents many common errors before they occur.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "command/pre/$CLAUDE_TIMESTAMP" --value "$CLAUDE_COMMAND" --namespace "commands" --batch true
hooks._comment: Stores the command in memory before execution, creating an audit trail and allowing the neural optimization system to learn from both successful and failed commands.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural predict --model "error_preventer" --input "$CLAUDE_COMMAND" --block-if-risky true --cache true
hooks._comment: Uses the error prevention neural model to predict if this command might fail or cause problems. If the risk score is too high, the command can be blocked and the user prompted for confirmation.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha hooks pre-edit --file "$CLAUDE_EDITED_FILE" --auto-assign-agents true --load-context true --analyze-impact true --batch true --cache true
hooks._comment: Before editing any file, this hook automatically assigns appropriate agents based on file type, loads relevant context from memory, and analyzes the potential impact of changes. This helps maintain code quality and prevents breaking changes.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "edit/pre/$CLAUDE_EDITED_FILE" --value "$CLAUDE_OPERATION_CONTEXT" --namespace "edits" --batch true
hooks._comment: Stores edit context before changes occur, enabling rollback and helping the system learn which types of edits are most successful.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural optimize --operation "file-edit" --target "$CLAUDE_EDITED_FILE" --suggest-improvements true --cache true
hooks._comment: Neural optimization analyzes the planned edit and suggests improvements based on past successful patterns, code style guidelines, and best practices for the specific file type.

hooks.command: /bin/bash -c 'FILE=$(cat | jq -r ".tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.path // empty"); if [ -n "$FILE" ]; then CHECKPOINT_BRANCH="checkpoint/pre-edit-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"; git add -A && git stash push -m "Pre-edit checkpoint for $FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && git branch "$CHECKPOINT_BRANCH" && mkdir -p .claude/checkpoints && echo "{\"branch\": \"$CHECKPOINT_BRANCH\", \"file\": \"$FILE\", \"timestamp\": \"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\", \"type\": \"pre-edit\", \"original_branch\": \"$(git branch --show-current)\"}" > ".claude/checkpoints/$(date +%s).json" && git stash pop --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1 || true && echo "✅ Created checkpoint: $CHECKPOINT_BRANCH for $FILE"; fi'
hooks._comment: Creates a Git checkpoint before editing, allowing instant rollback if the edit causes problems. Checkpoints are organized by timestamp and stored as both branches and JSON metadata files for easy recovery.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "todos/$(date +%s)" --value "$CLAUDE_TODOS" --namespace "tasks" --batch true
hooks._comment: Stores TODO items in memory so they can be tracked, prioritized, and referenced by agents working on related tasks.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural predict --model "task_predictor" --input "$CLAUDE_TODOS" --optimize-order true --cache true
hooks._comment: Neural prediction analyzes TODO items to suggest optimal ordering based on dependencies, complexity, and historical patterns of what order tends to work best for similar task sets.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha hooks post-command --command "$CLAUDE_COMMAND" --track-metrics true --store-results true --analyze-performance true --batch true
hooks._comment: After command execution, this hook tracks performance metrics (execution time, success/failure, resource usage), stores results for future reference, and analyzes performance to identify optimization opportunities.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "command/post/$CLAUDE_TIMESTAMP" --value "{\"command\": \"$CLAUDE_COMMAND\", \"result\": \"$CLAUDE_RESULT\", \"duration\": $CLAUDE_DURATION}" --namespace "commands" --batch true
hooks._comment: Stores command results with performance data, building a historical database that helps predict future execution times and identify performance regressions.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural train --model "performance_optimizer" --data "{\"operation\": \"bash\", \"duration\": $CLAUDE_DURATION, \"success\": $CLAUDE_SUCCESS}" --batch true
hooks._comment: Trains the performance optimizer model with actual execution data, allowing it to learn which commands are fast/slow, which succeed/fail, and patterns that predict outcomes.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha hooks post-edit --file "$CLAUDE_EDITED_FILE" --format true --update-memory true --train-neural true --analyze-quality true
hooks._comment: After editing, this hook automatically formats the file according to project standards, updates memory with the changes, trains neural models to learn from the edit pattern, and analyzes code quality to ensure standards are maintained.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "edit/post/{}" --value '{"changes": $CLAUDE_CHANGES, "quality_score": $CLAUDE_QUALITY_SCORE}' --namespace "edits" --batch true
hooks._comment: Stores edit outcomes with quality scoring, helping the system learn what constitutes high-quality code changes and avoid patterns that historically produce bugs or maintenance issues.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural train --model "task_predictor" --data '{"file_type": "$CLAUDE_FILE_TYPE", "operation": "$CLAUDE_OPERATION", "success": true}' --batch true
hooks._comment: Trains the task predictor to understand which types of operations work well for different file types, improving future task assignment and agent selection.

hooks.command: /bin/bash -c 'FILE=$(cat | jq -r ".tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.path // empty"); if [ -n "$FILE" ] && [ -f "$FILE" ]; then if ! git ls-files --error-unmatch "$FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then git add "$FILE"; fi; if ! (git diff --cached --quiet "$FILE" 2>/dev/null && git diff --quiet "$FILE" 2>/dev/null); then TAG_NAME="checkpoint-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"; BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current); git add "$FILE" && git commit -m "🔖 Checkpoint: Edit $FILE" --quiet && git tag -a "$TAG_NAME" -m "Checkpoint after editing $FILE" && mkdir -p .claude/checkpoints && DIFF_STATS=$(git diff HEAD~1 --stat | tr "\n" " " | sed "s/\"/\\\\\"/g") && echo "{\"tag\": \"$TAG_NAME\", \"file\": \"$FILE\", \"timestamp\": \"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\", \"type\": \"post-edit\", \"branch\": \"$BRANCH\", \"diff_summary\": \"$DIFF_STATS\"}" > ".claude/checkpoints/$(date +%s).json" && echo "✅ Created checkpoint: $TAG_NAME for $FILE"; else echo "ℹ️  No changes to checkpoint for $FILE"; fi; fi'
hooks._comment: Creates a post-edit checkpoint with Git commit and tag, storing diff statistics and metadata. This provides granular rollback points for every file modification.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "task/complete/$CLAUDE_TASK_ID" --value '{"task": "$CLAUDE_TASK", "agent": "$CLAUDE_AGENT", "result": "$CLAUDE_RESULT"}' --namespace "tasks"
hooks._comment: Stores completed task information with the agent that handled it and the result, building a knowledge base of which agents excel at which types of tasks.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural train --model "task_predictor" --data '{"task_type": "$CLAUDE_TASK_TYPE", "agent_type": "$CLAUDE_AGENT_TYPE", "performance": $CLAUDE_PERFORMANCE}'
hooks._comment: Trains the task predictor to improve future task-to-agent assignments based on historical performance data.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "prompt/$(date +%s)" --value "$CLAUDE_PROMPT" --namespace "prompts"
hooks._comment: Stores user prompts for pattern analysis and to help the system understand common request types and optimal responses.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural analyze --prompt "$CLAUDE_PROMPT" --suggest-approach true --predict-complexity true
hooks._comment: Neural analysis of the prompt suggests the best approach to take (single agent vs swarm, which tools to use, estimated complexity) before any work begins.

hooks.command:
/bin/bash -c 'TASK=$(echo "{{user_prompt}}" | head -c 100 | tr "\n" " "); if [ -n "$TASK" ]; then CHECKPOINT_NAME="task-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"; git add -A && git commit -m "🔖 Task checkpoint: $TASK..." --quiet || true; if command -v gh &> /dev/null; then echo "🚀 Creating GitHub release for checkpoint..."; gh release create "$CHECKPOINT_NAME" --title "Checkpoint: $(date +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")" --notes "Task: $TASK

## Checkpoint Details
- Branch: $(git branch --show-current)
- Commit: $(git rev-parse HEAD)
- Files changed: $(git diff HEAD~1 --stat 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo 0) files

## Rollback Instructions
\`\`\`bash
# To rollback to this checkpoint:
git checkout $CHECKPOINT_NAME
\`\`\`" --prerelease || echo "⚠️  Failed to create GitHub release"; fi; mkdir -p .claude/checkpoints && echo "{\"checkpoint\": \"$CHECKPOINT_NAME\", \"task\": \"$TASK\", \"timestamp\": \"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\", \"commit\": \"$(git rev-parse HEAD)\", \"github_release\": \"$(command -v gh &> /dev/null && echo true || echo false)\"}" > ".claude/checkpoints/task-$(date +%s).json" && echo "✅ Created task checkpoint: $CHECKPOINT_NAME"; fi'
hooks._comment: Creates a task-level checkpoint when a new user prompt is submitted, providing a recovery point if the task doesn't go as planned. Optionally creates GitHub releases for major checkpoints.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end --generate-summary true --persist-state true --export-metrics true --backup-memory true --optimize-models true
hooks._comment: When a session ends, this comprehensive hook generates a summary of what was accomplished, persists all state to disk, exports performance metrics for analysis, backs up all memory systems, and optimizes neural models with the session's learning data.

hooks.command:
/bin/bash -c 'SESSION_ID="session-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"; SUMMARY_FILE=".claude/checkpoints/summary-$SESSION_ID.md"; mkdir -p .claude/checkpoints && echo "# Session Summary - $(date +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

## Checkpoints Created
$(find .claude/checkpoints -name "*.json" -mtime -1 -exec basename {} \; | sort)

## Files Modified
$(git diff --name-only $(git log --format=%H -n 1 --before="1 hour ago" 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null || echo "No files tracked")

## Recent Commits
$(git log --oneline -10 --grep="Checkpoint" || echo "No checkpoint commits")

## GitHub Releases Created
$(gh release list --limit 10 | grep "checkpoint-" || echo "No GitHub releases")

## Rollback Instructions
To rollback to a specific checkpoint:
\`\`\`bash
# List all checkpoints
git tag -l "checkpoint-*" | sort -r

# List GitHub releases
gh release list

# Rollback to a checkpoint
git checkout checkpoint-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS
\`\`\`" > "$SUMMARY_FILE" && git add -A && git commit -m "🏁 Session end checkpoint: $SESSION_ID" --quiet || true && git tag -a "session-end-$SESSION_ID" -m "End of Claude session" && if command -v gh &> /dev/null; then echo "📊 Creating GitHub session summary..."; gh release create "session-$SESSION_ID" --title "Session Summary: $(date +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")" --notes-file "$SUMMARY_FILE" --prerelease || echo "⚠️  Failed to create GitHub session summary"; fi && echo "✅ Session summary saved to: $SUMMARY_FILE" && echo "📌 Final checkpoint: session-end-$SESSION_ID"'
hooks._comment: Creates a comprehensive session summary document listing all checkpoints created, files modified, commits made, and providing clear rollback instructions. This serves as both documentation and disaster recovery guide.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory backup --namespace "all" --destination ".claude/memory-backup-$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID.json"
hooks._comment: Backs up all memory systems to a timestamped JSON file, ensuring no learning or context is lost between sessions.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural train --model "all" --data "session" --comprehensive true
hooks._comment: Comprehensive neural model training at session end incorporates all the learning from the entire session, potentially discovering patterns that weren't visible from individual operations.

hooks.command: git add .claude/memory-backup-*.json && git commit -m "🧠 Session memory backup: $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID" || true
hooks._comment: Commits memory backups to Git, providing version control for learned patterns and enabling recovery of memory state from any point in project history.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha github create-gist --name "session-learnings-$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID" --content "$CLAUDE_SESSION_LEARNINGS" --private true || true
hooks._comment: Creates a private GitHub Gist containing key learnings from the session, providing a shareable but secure way to document insights and patterns discovered.

checkpoint._comment: Automatic checkpoints every 5 minutes (300 seconds) ensure regular recovery points even during long-running operations. This interval balances protection against Git history bloat.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha checkpoint create --message "Auto-checkpoint: $CLAUDE_OPERATIONS_COUNT operations" --include-memory true
hooks._comment: Creates a checkpoint with current operation count and full memory state, enabling precise recovery to any point in time.

hooks.command: git add -A && git commit -m "🔄 Auto-checkpoint: $(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" || true
hooks._comment: Git commit for the auto-checkpoint, ensuring the working tree state is captured.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory sync --remote true --compress true
hooks._comment: Syncs memory to remote storage (if configured) with compression, providing off-site backup of learned patterns.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha memory store --key "error/$CLAUDE_ERROR_ID" --value '{"error": "$CLAUDE_ERROR", "context": "$CLAUDE_ERROR_CONTEXT"}' --namespace "errors"
hooks._comment: Stores error information with full context, building a knowledge base of what went wrong and why. This helps prevent the same errors from recurring.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha neural train --model "error_preventer" --data '{"error_type": "$CLAUDE_ERROR_TYPE", "operation": "$CLAUDE_OPERATION", "prevent": true}'
hooks._comment: Trains the error prevention model to recognize patterns that lead to this type of error, improving future error prediction and prevention.

hooks.command: npx claude-flow@alpha analysis error-pattern --error "$CLAUDE_ERROR" --suggest-fix true --store-pattern true
hooks._comment: Analyzes the error pattern, suggests potential fixes based on similar past errors, and stores the pattern for future reference.

hooks.command: /bin/bash -c 'INPUT=$(cat); CUSTOM=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r ".custom_instructions // \"\""); echo "🔄 PreCompact Guidance:"; echo "📋 IMPORTANT: Review CLAUDE.md in project root for:"; echo "   • 54 available agents and concurrent usage patterns"; echo "   • Swarm coordination strategies (hierarchical, mesh, adaptive)"; echo "   • SPARC methodology workflows with batchtools optimization"; echo "   • Critical concurrent execution rules (GOLDEN RULE: 1 MESSAGE = ALL OPERATIONS)"; if [ -n "$CUSTOM" ]; then echo "🎯 Custom compact instructions: $CUSTOM"; fi; echo "✅ Ready for compact operation"'
hooks._comment: Before manual compaction, reminds you of key information from CLAUDE.md to ensure context isn't lost when the conversation history is compressed. This is crucial for maintaining awareness of available agents and coordination patterns.

hooks.command: /bin/bash -c 'echo "🔄 Auto-Compact Guidance (Context Window Full):"; echo "📋 CRITICAL: Before compacting, ensure you understand:"; echo "   • All 54 agents available in .claude/agents/ directory"; echo "   • Concurrent execution patterns from CLAUDE.md"; echo "   • Batchtools optimization for 300% performance gains"; echo "   • Swarm coordination strategies for complex tasks"; echo "⚡ Apply GOLDEN RULE: Always batch operations in single messages"; echo "✅ Auto-compact proceeding with full agent context"'
hooks._comment: When auto-compaction triggers (context window is full), provides critical reminders about agent capabilities and optimization patterns to preserve across the compaction boundary.

neural._comment_neural: Neural optimization is a key differentiator in this configuration. The system uses WebAssembly-powered neural networks to learn from every operation, predict outcomes, prevent errors, and optimize performance. This happens continuously in the background, making the system progressively smarter over time without manual intervention.

task_predictor._comment: Predicts task completion time, optimal agent assignment, and resource requirements based on historical patterns.

error_preventer._comment: Analyzes planned operations for error patterns and blocks potentially problematic commands before execution.

performance_optimizer._comment: Continuously tunes system parameters to optimize for speed, accuracy, and resource efficiency based on workload patterns.

wasm._comment: WebAssembly configuration for neural networks provides near-native performance for model inference and training, critical for real-time optimization.

statusLine._comment: Custom status line script can display current memory usage, active agents, pending tasks, and other relevant state information.

mcpServers._comment_mcp_servers: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers provide tool interfaces for external systems. Each server exposes a set of tools that Claude can use to interact with memory systems, orchestrators, and other services. The stdio type means the server communicates via standard input/output pipes, which is lightweight and secure.

claude-flow._comment: Primary orchestration server providing task management, agent coordination, and workflow execution tools.

ruv-swarm._comment: Distributed swarm coordination server for multi-agent task execution with WASM-powered performance.

letta._comment: Agent memory management server providing core/archival memory operations for stateful agents.

openmemory._comment: User personalization server providing cross-application profile management and preference storage.

ruvector._comment: High-performance vector search server for semantic code search, pattern matching, and similarity queries.

graphiti._comment: Temporal knowledge graph server for tracking entity relationships and state changes over time.

_final_notes.memory_system_overview: This configuration integrates five specialized memory systems working together: RuVector for fast vector search across your codebase, Letta for maintaining agent state and personas, Graphiti for temporal knowledge graphs tracking how borrower and loan information evolves, FalkorDB as the graph database backend, and Mem0/OpenMemory for user personalization that follows borrowers across your applications. Each system has a specific role and they coordinate through the memory.systems.coordination section.
_final_notes.performance_philosophy: The performance configuration is designed around the principle that your three GPU workers (48GB, 24GB, 12GB VRAM) should handle 95%+ of AI workload, with cloud APIs only as fallback for critical operations requiring maximum accuracy. Aggressive caching, batching, and parallel execution minimize both API costs and latency.
_final_notes.hooks_learning_loop: The hooks system creates a continuous learning loop where every operation teaches the neural models to be better. PreToolUse hooks predict and prevent errors, PostToolUse hooks measure and optimize performance, error hooks prevent recurrence, and session end hooks consolidate all learning. This makes the system progressively smarter without manual intervention.
_final_notes.checkpoint_safety_net: Multiple layers of checkpoints provide comprehensive safety: per-operation checkpoints before risky changes, periodic auto-checkpoints every 5 minutes, task-level checkpoints when new work begins, and session-end checkpoints with full summaries. Combined with Git integration and optional GitHub release creation, you can recover from any point in time.
_final_notes.mortgage_specific_optimizations: The configuration includes mortgage-specific agent types (mortgage-specialist, compliance-checker, document-processor), memory namespaces (borrowers, loans, campaigns, conversations), and integration points for CRM, drip campaigns, and quote engines. This ensures the system understands mortgage domain concepts and can maintain context across the entire loan lifecycle.
